    The extension commutes with filtered colimits and direct sums #

    If Φ : D_fin → mod A is exact, then its colimit extension F = Extension.functor Φ : D → Mod A commutes with filtered colimits, and, if Φ is moreover additive, with arbitrary direct sums.

          A functor preserving finite coproducts and filtered colimits preserves all coproducts: an arbitrary coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite subcoproducts.

          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Extension.preservesCoproducts {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type u} [Ring A] {Φ : CategoryTheory.Functor (Dfin k) (ModuleCat A)} [Φ.Additive] (hexact : IsExactOnDfin Φ) (ι : Type u) :
          CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape (CategoryTheory.Discrete ι) (functor Φ)

          The extension F of an additive exact Φ commutes with arbitrary direct sums. As in the manuscript, an arbitrary sum is the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, and F preserves finite sums by additivity.
